{{Short description|Private prison in Georgia, US}}
{{Use American English|date=August 2025}}
[[File:Map of Georgia highlighting Irwin County.svg|thumb|205x205px|Irwin County Georgia where the Irwin County Detention Center is located.]]
The '''Irwin County Detention Center,''' located in [[Ocilla, Georgia]] is privately owned by Louisiana-based LaSalle Corrections. In 2010, [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] (ICE) contracted to use the facility as an [[Immigration detention in the United States|immigrant detention]] center and renewed its contract with LaSalle in 2019 at a rate for each immigrant of $71.29 a day. The detention center lost its contract in 2021 with the government after a series of human rights violations in 2020. At least 43 women prisoners and a [[whistleblower]] nurse came forward alleging that [[non-consensual surgeries]] and [[medically unnecessary]] procedures, including [[hysterectomy|hysterectomies]], were performed by a gynecologist affiliated with the jail.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gabbatt |first1=Adam |date=November 21, 2020 |title='He hurt me': migrants who accused Ice gynecologist of abuse speak out |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2020/nov/21/congress-ice-gynecologist-abuse-allegations-petition |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220413205235/https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2020/nov/21/congress-ice-gynecologist-abuse-allegations-petition |archive-date=April 13, 2022 |access-date=April 13, 2022 |work=The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Alvarez |first=Priscilla |date=September 16, 2020 |title=Whistleblower alleges high rate of hysterectomies and medical neglect at ICE facility |url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/09/15/politics/immigration-customs-enforcement-medical-care-detainees/index.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200919153830/https://www.cnn.com/2020/09/15/politics/immigration-customs-enforcement-medical-care-detainees/index.html |archive-date=September 19, 2020 |access-date=September 19, 2020 |publisher=CNN}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Olivares |first1=José |last2=Washington |first2=John |date=September 15, 2020 |title='He Just Empties You All Out': |publisher=The Intercept}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Olivares |first1=José |last2=Washington |first2=John |date=September 14, 2020 |title='A Silent Pandemic': Nurse at Ice Facility Blows the Whistle |publisher=The Intercept}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Lambe |first=Jerry |date=September 14, 2020 |title='Like an Experimental Concentration Camp': Whistleblower Complaint Alleges Mass Hysterectomies |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200917195840/https://lawandcrime.com/high-profile/like-an-experimental-concentration-camp-whistleblower-complaint-alleges-mass-hysterectomies-at-ice-detention-center/ |archive-date=September 17, 2020 |access-date=September 17, 2020 |publisher=[[Law & Crime]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=O'Toole |first=Molly |date=October 22, 2020 |title=19 women allege medical abuse in Georgia immigration detention |url=https://www.latimes.com/politics/story/2020-10-22/women-allege-medical-abuse-georgia-immigration-detention |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201024213542/https://www.latimes.com/politics/story/2020-10-22/women-allege-medical-abuse-georgia-immigration-detention |archive-date=2020-10-24 |access-date=2020-10-24 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> The women also complained of retaliation and subpar [[COVID-19]] treatment. On December 22, 2020, forty migrant women being held at the Irwin County Detention Center filed a lawsuit alleging abuse and unnecessary forced medical procedures, including the hysterectomies.<ref name="lawsuit2">{{cite news |last1=Castronuovo |first1=Celine |date=December 22, 2020 |title=Migrant women file lawsuit against doctor for alleged forced medical procedures |url=https://thehill.com/latino/531285-migrant-women-file-lawsuit-against-doctor-for-alleged-forced-medical-procedures?fbclid=IwAR2QsmYq70JtYJBKNvkRzOOq7ju-oTKm2n6oCLMnxB3DNrQvvgqN9TQW0EI |access-date=December 22, 2020 |work=The Hill |language=en}}</ref>

In 2021, the court case, Oldaker v. Giles and an investigation conducted by the US Senate led to the termination of the US government's contract with the detention center.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |title=Oldaker v. Giles – Clinic represents survivors of alleged medical abuse suffered while in ICE custody – First Amendment Clinic |url=https://firstamendment.law.uga.edu/work/oldaker-v-giles/ |access-date=2024-10-26 |website=firstamendment.law.uga.edu}}</ref><ref name="Sacchetti-Wapo2">{{cite news |last1=Sacchetti |first1=Maria |date=May 20, 2021 |title=ICE to stop detaining immigrants at two county jails under federal investigation |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/immigration/ice-detentions-county-jails-halted/2021/05/20/9c0bdd1e-b8de-11eb-a6b1-81296da0339b_story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220405005610/https://www.washingtonpost.com/immigration/ice-detentions-county-jails-halted/2021/05/20/9c0bdd1e-b8de-11eb-a6b1-81296da0339b_story.html |archive-date=5 April 2022 |access-date=12 April 2022 |newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref> In January 2025, the case was settled to the parties’ mutual satisfaction.
By October 2025 however, ICE renewed a contract  with Irwin County Detention Center.

==History==
The Irwin County Detention Center is a 1296-bed jail located in [[Ocilla, Georgia]] and owned privately owned by Louisiana-based LaSalle Corrections.<ref>{{cite web |last=Clarke |first=Matthew |date=February 15, 2013 |title=LaSalle Corrections: A Family-Run Prison Firm |url=https://www.prisonlegalnews.org/news/2013/feb/15/lasalle-corrections-a-family-run-prison-firm/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201117105138/https://www.prisonlegalnews.org/news/2013/feb/15/lasalle-corrections-a-family-run-prison-firm/ |archive-date=November 17, 2020 |access-date=November 12, 2020 |newspaper=[[Prison Legal News]]}}</ref> In 2010, [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] (ICE) contracted to use the facility as an [[Immigration detention in the United States|immigrant detention]] center.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last1=Ghandakly |first1=Elizabeth C |last2=Fabi |first2=Rachel |title=Sterilization in US Immigration and Customs Enforcement's (ICE's) Detention: Ethical Failures and Systemic Injustice |journal=American Journal of Public Health |date=2021 |volume=111 |issue=5 |pages=832–834 |doi=10.2105/AJPH.2021.306186 |pmid=33826372 |pmc=8034024 }}</ref>
It renewed the contract in 2019 at a rate of $71.29 per immigrant per day.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Hernández |first=César Cuauhtémoc García |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=LyKtEAAAQBAJ&dq=dawn+wooten&pg=PT66 |title=Welcome the Wretched: In Defense of the "Criminal Alien" |date=2024-01-30 |publisher=The New Press |isbn=978-1-62097-830-6 |language=en}}</ref>

===  Allegations in 2016===
Concerns about the Irwin County Detention Center (IDC) had been raised in a 2016 report to a Department of Homeland Security committee; it indicated that there was a failure to provide sufficient medical care to immigrant detainees.<ref name=":0"/> In 2017, [[Project South (organization)|Project South]], an Atlanta-based grassroots organization, and Penn State published a report on the conditions at two Georgia immigration centers: [[Stewart Detention Center]] and Irwin County Detention Center. The report highlighted issues detainees faced such as overcrowded housing, unhygienic living conditions, and lack of legal access.<ref>{{Cite journal |title=Imprisoned Justice: Inside Two Georgia Immigrant Detention Centers |url=https://projectsouth.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Imprisoned_Justice_Report-1.pdf |journal=Project South}}</ref> Concerns were brought to the media's attention in 2019 when famous rapper [[21 Savage]], a British national, was detained in the Irwin Detention Center for a week. ICE renewed its contract with LaSalle in 2019 paying $71.29 per immigrant daily. The average number of immigrants at Irwin during 2019 was 848 making their average income $2.9 million a week. Despite the money sent to Irwin the healthcare continued to be poor leading to further allegations in 2020.<ref name=":0" />

Dr. Mahendra Amin, the gynecologist at the facility also had a “history of medical malpractice suits filed against him.”<ref name=":12"/> This included fraudulent [[Medicaid]] claims. This dispute was settled by a payment of over half a million dollars. This was paid for by Amin and eight fellow doctors at Irwin County Hospital.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Lenzer |first=Jeanne |date=2020 |title="Mass hysterectomies" were carried out on migrants in US detention centre, claims whistleblower |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/27239068 |journal=BMJ: British Medical Journal |volume=370 |pages=1–2 |jstor=27239068 |issn=0959-8138}}</ref>

=== Allegations in 2020 ===
On September 14, 2020, Dawn Wooten, a licensed nurse who worked at the Irwin County Detention Center, filed a whistleblower complaint against the facility. She was represented by [[Project South (organization)|Project South]], Georgia Detention Watch, the Georgia Latino Alliance for Human Rights, and the South Georgia Immigrant Support Network.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Bhatt |first1=Priyanka |last2=Quigley |first2=Katie |last3=Shahshahani |first3=Azadeh |last4=Starfield |first4=Gina |last5=Kitano |first5=Ayano |date=September 2021 |title=Violence and Violation: Medical Abuse of Immigrants Detained at the Irwin Country Detention Center |url=https://projectsouth.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/IrwinReport_14SEPT21.pdf |website=Project South}}</ref>
[[File:Irwin_County_Hospital.JPG|thumb|256x256px|Irwin County Hospital where immigrant detainees were taken off site to be treated.]]
The reports focused extensively on the detention center's failure to comply with the appropriate [[COVID-19]] protocol,  including the lack of quarantine for new arrivals, little to no treatment for detainees with symptoms, and fabricated medical records.<ref name=":3"/><ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last=Jennings |first=Helen |date=Fall 2021 |title="He's the Uterus Collector": The Reproductive Rights of Women in Ice Detention; An Opportunity to Protect the Constitutional Rights of Federal Detainees in Privately Run Facilities. |url=https://go.gale.com/ps/retrieve.do?tabID=T002&resultListType=RESULT_LIST&searchResultsType=SingleTab&retrievalId=902c9a2a-bcd9-4de4-b2cb-59a48191934f&hitCount=1&searchType=AdvancedSearchForm&currentPosition=1&docId=GALE%7CA698998984&docType=Article&sort=RELEVANCE&contentSegment=ZONE-MOD1&prodId=AONE&pageNum=1&contentSet=GALE%7CA698998984&searchId=R5&userGroupName=byuprovo&inPS=true&aty=ip |journal=Georgetown Journal of Gender and the Law |volume=23 |issue=1 |via=Gale Academic Onefile}}</ref>

Another complaint was the violation of [[informed consent]] as outlined in the [[ICE Performance-Based National Detention Standards of 2011|ICE National Detention Standards]]. It was reported that [[Google Translate]] or other inmates were used to provide translation of information about medical procedures leading to miscommunications, including women receiving [[Hysterectomy|hysterectomies.]]<ref name=":3" /> The report stated that women were receiving these hysterectomies without their knowledge. Whistleblower Dawn Wooten would even label Dr. Mahendra Amin as the “Uterus Collector."<ref name=":6">{{Cite book |last=Herrera |first=Alexandria |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1353/book.119911 |title=Resistance and Abolition in the Borderlands |date=2024 |publisher=University of Arizona Press |isbn=978-0-8165-5233-7 |chapter=Chapter 4: The Uterus Collectors: The Lineage of Hemispheric Medical Abuse and Experimentation in the United States and Guatemala|doi=10.1353/book.119911 }}</ref> The title of “uterus collector” and nonconsensual reproductive procedures led this event to be widely publicized.<ref name=":7">{{Cite news |last=O'Toole |first=Molly |date=22 October 2020 |title=19 Women Allege Medical Abuse in Georgia Immigration Detention |url=https://www.latimes.com/politics/story/2020-10-22/women-allege-medical-abuse-georgia-immigration-detention |access-date=26 October 2024 |newspaper=LA Times}}</ref> While there were only three pages regarding these gynecological procedures in the initial report, these allegations were the most widely publicized.<ref name=":4" />

Throughout these events Dr. Amin maintained his innocence with his lawyer stating, “that Dr. Amin always acted appropriately with patients, obtained informed consent, and used translators/interpreters whenever necessary."<ref name=":7" />

Female detainees had actively tried to advocate for themselves, even creating a YouTube video about their experiences.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aQt6QbkWsLI |title=Women at Irwin County Detention Center in GA Fight for Their Lives Against COVID19 4/13/2020 |date=2020-04-13 |last=Rachel Taber |access-date=2024-11-29 |via=YouTube}}</ref> Attempts to report the abuse led to punishment, including [[solitary confinement]], transfer of unit, and even [[physical assault]].<ref name=":2"/> [[Hunger strike]]s were met with rationed food, stolen money, and restricted technology use.<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal |last=Torres |first=Lizet Palomera |date=September 2023 |title=A Vicious Cycle: United States' Failure to Protect Immigrant Women's Reproductive Rights at the Irwin County Detention Center |url=https://go.gale.com/ps/i.do?p=AONE&u=byuprovo&v=2.1&it=r&id=GALE%7CA775899637&retrievalId=d48273df-294d-49ab-9461-cc6fc93eaf2a&inPS=true&linkSource=interlink&sid=bookmark-AONE |journal=Golden Gate University Law Review |volume=53 |issue=2 |via=Gale Academic Onefile}}</ref>

=== Oldaker v. Giles ===
On December 21, 2020, the National Immigration Project of the [[National Lawyers Guild]] (NIPNLG), [[David Dreyer]], Project South as well as law school clinics from [[Harvard University|Harvard]], [[University of Georgia School of Law|University of Georgia]], [[Columbia University|Columbia]], [[Texas A&M University|Texas A&M]], and [[Boston University]] filed litigation for fourteen women who had been detained in ICDC. The case included more than forty testimonies from women detailing medical abuses happening at ICDC.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-05 |title=Oldaker v. Giles {{!}} NIPNLG |url=https://nipnlg.org/work/litigation/oldaker-v-giles |access-date=2024-11-29 |website=nipnlg.org |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":12"/>

The court case included a filing that resulted in the release of custody for the women involved in the case. On January 22, 2021, all of the women from the case were released from the Irwin County Detention Center to their families, but they were still under the supervision of ICE.<ref name=":12"/><ref>{{cite news |last=Redmon |first=Jeremy |date=September 4, 2021 |title=All ICE detainees moved out of South Georgia jail |url=https://www.ajc.com/news/all-ice-detainees-moved-out-of-south-georgia-jail/XJ6XIUTVBFCN3IALTUCUFUNBX4/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220122161506/https://www.ajc.com/news/all-ice-detainees-moved-out-of-south-georgia-jail/XJ6XIUTVBFCN3IALTUCUFUNBX4/ |archive-date=January 22, 2022 |access-date=January 22, 2022 |newspaper=[[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]}}</ref>

In response to the case and ongoing advocacy work, the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Joe Biden administration]] announced severance with the Irwin Detention Center in May 2021 and all detainees were relocated to other facilities by September 3, 2021. The severance was legally enforced on October 7th, 2021 with the official termination of ICE's contract with the Irwin County Detention Center.<ref name=":12"/>

Under supplemental jurisdiction, the Federal Court can handle state claims related to the case even if those claims fall outside the court's usual authority. However, in this case, the federal court chose not to exercise this power, leading to the dismissal of all defendants besides the United States. The plaintiff's counsel proceeded with the case, asserting that the 2020 medical abuse claims from the ICDC fall under the [[Federal Tort Claims Act]].<ref name=":12"/> 
In January 2025, the case was settled to the parties’ mutual satisfaction.<ref name=":12"/>

=== U.S. Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, 2022 ===
In 2022, the United States Senate's Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, released a 103-page report after it investigated the Irwin Detention Center.<ref name=":8">{{Cite magazine |last=Aguilera |first=Jasmine |date=2022-11-16 |title=Senate Committee Finds Medical Abuse of Detained Women at Georgia ICE Facility |url=https://time.com/6234031/medical-abuse-georgia-women-detained/ |access-date=2024-10-23 |magazine=TIME |language=en}}</ref> It was released two years after the 2020 allegations on November 15, 2022.<ref name=":12"/> Senator Jon Ossoff and [[Ron Johnson|Senator Ron Johnson]] led this 18-month bipartisan investigation. Throughout the inquiry, Dr. Amin fervently denied the allegations and refused to appear before the committee. However, the investigation discovered a “history of medical malpractice suits filed against him.” While Dr. Amin only treated 6.5% of ICDC detainees, he performed 94% of the laparoscopies.<ref name=":12"/> The committee concluded that the women at the detention center, “appear to have been subjected to excessive, invasive, and often unnecessary gynecological procedures.”<ref name=":8" /> However, the allegation spread across news headlines that Dr. Amin performed unrequired hysterectomies was found false stating, “The Subcommittee found this allegation to be false, and ICE determined that the two hysterectomies Dr. Amin performed on ICDC detainees appeared to be medically necessary.”<ref name=":8" />

Karina Cisneros Preciado's November 2022 testimony before the subcommittee was widely published. Preciado had been separated from her newborn child when she was placed in ICDC. While there, her postpartum care was delayed despite experiencing pain. She was eventually taken off-site to Dr. Amin where she received an unexplained vaginal ultrasound despite being told she was being taken for a pap smear. The result of the visit was a [[Medroxyprogesterone acetate|Depo-Provera]] shot for a supposed [[ovarian cyst]]. She was informed that if the shot failed, she would need to undergo surgery. Such a surgery was prevented as allegations of abuse surfaced before her return.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mukherjee |first1=Elora |last2=Marouf |first2=Fatma |last3=Ardalan |first3=Sabrineh |date=2024 |title=Congress's Untapped Authority to Certify U Visas |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/27305118 |journal=Columbia Law Review |volume=124 |issue=2 |pages=43–66 |jstor=27305118 |issn=0010-1958}}</ref>

=== Defamation lawsuit, 2024 ===
Dr. Amin filed a defamation lawsuit which was set to be heard in April 2025. He was suing [[NBCUniversal|NBCUniversal Media]] for claiming that he performed, “massed hysterectomies” and [[Wondery]] for labelling him as a “uterus collector.” He was suing them for a combined total of $45 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pearson |first=Emily Wu |date=2024-08-01 |title=Doctor accused of abuse at defunct Georgia detention center seeks $45 million for defamation |url=https://www.wabe.org/doctor-accused-of-abuse-at-defunct-georgia-detention-center-seeks-45-million-for-defamation/ |access-date=2024-10-23 |website=WABE |language=en-US}}</ref> The lawsuit was settled in February 2025 with U.S. District Judge Lisa Godbey Wood commenting that "undisputed evidence has established" that "there were no mass hysterectomies or high numbers of hysterectomies at the facility" <ref>{{Cite news |last=Folkenflik |first=David |date=2025-02-21 |title=NBC settles defamation lawsuit with doctor falsely labeled "uterus collector" |url=https://www.npr.org/2025/02/21/nx-s1-5305268/nbc-settles-lawsuit-ice-doctor-msnbc-maddow-georgia-detainee |access-date=2025-04-11 |work=NPR |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

=== Dawn Wooten ===
Dawn Wooten, now known as the ICE [[whistleblower]], had seen the COVID violations and became more alarmed as women began to describe experiences of uninformed sterility. In 2020, Wooten reported these issues to her supervisors, leading to her demotion to an on-call position. Following the demotion, she was not called to fulfill any further shifts at the center, and although she was never formally terminated, she was effectively side-lined. Wooten struggled to secure further employment due to her publicity, which affected her and her family.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bryant |first=Miranda |date=2022-10-17 |title='I'm back on food stamps': Nurse who exposed 'uterus collector' still faces consequences |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2022/oct/17/whistleblower-uterus-collector-repercussions-ice-detained-immigrant-women |access-date=2024-11-29 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite web |date=2022-10-04 |title=Nurse Dawn Wooten |url=https://whistleblower.org/whistleblower-profiles/nurse-dawn-wooten/ |access-date=2024-10-26 |website=Government Accountability Project |language=en-US}}</ref>

Wooten would eventually be represented by Project South and the [[Government Accountability Project]] when she made the whistleblower complaints in 2020. She would continue to advocate for her patients calling for congressional action. For her advocacy Wooten has won many awards including the 2021 Joe Callaway Award for Civic Courage, the Feleta Wilson Award, the 2022 Physicians for Human Rights Award, and the 2022 HMH Foundation First Amendment Award. The [[Giraffe Heroes Project]] named her as a Giraffe Hero<ref>{{cite web |title=Dawn Wooten - Giraffe Hero |url=https://giraffeheroes.org/1446/DawnWooten |website=giraffeheroes.org |publisher=[[Giraffe Heroes Project]] |access-date=11 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211112343/https://giraffeheroes.org/1446/DawnWooten |archive-date=11 December 2024 |language=en}}</ref> and she was also portrayed in the Americans Who Tell Truth Portrait series.<ref name=":9" />

===2025===
In October 2025 ICE renewed a contract with Irwin County Detention Center.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ICE has restarted detention in controversial South Georgia immigrant jail |url=https://www.ajc.com/news/2025/10/ice-has-restarted-detention-in-controversial-south-georgia-immigrant-jail/ |access-date=2025-10-26 |website=ajc |language=en}}</ref>
